Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Rishi Patel (Redwood SE), Lina Gomez (Redwood SE), Maya Lin (HarborPay - Head of ML), Carlos Ruiz (HarborPay - Platform Eng), Priya Sharma (HarborPay - CTO)
summary: Redwood-led Optimize walkthrough focused on batching and KV/prefix cache recommendations, with cost model examples applied to HarborPay's estimated traffic. Customer is evaluating Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private for production; main concerns: latency SLOs (95th < 200ms), cost per 1M tokens, data residency, and integration effort. Agreed next steps: send pricing, run HarborPay traces through KV cache model, schedule pilot benchmark.
topics: KV/prefix cache behavior and hit-rate impact
Cost model: tokens/sec, effective tokens saved, cost per 1M tokens
transcript:
[00:00] Ava Martinez: okay, welcome everyone, thanks for making time, this is the Redwood Optimize walkthrough, we'll cover batching and the KV/prefix cache and then run through a quick cost model against the traffic profile you shared
[00:12] Maya Lin: thanks, yeah excited, we want to understand how much we can save and what the latency tradeoffs are
[00:20] Rishi Patel: cool, quick agenda, batching overview, prefix vs kv cache, a couple numbers, then Q&A and next steps
[00:30] Carlos Ruiz: just to flag, our 95th p95 SLO is 200 ms, if it goes over we get paged, so latency is huge for us
[00:40] Rishi Patel: totally makes sense, we'll show config that keeps p95 under target while reducing token cost
[01:05] Lina Gomez: quick note, HarborPay current stack: inference endpoints on-prem + some burst to AWS, roughly 2k qps at peak, average request length 120 tokens, convo-style prefix reuse across sessions
[01:22] Maya Lin: yep and many requests re-use the same initial prompt template and top-20 intents, so prefix caching seems promising
[01:35] Rishi Patel: perfect, that's exactly the use-case for our prefix/KV cache, so two levers: batching (to increase throughput and amortize kernel cost) and KV/prefix cache (to avoid re-computing early layers and tokens). We'll start with batching
[02:00] Rishi Patel: batching modes: micro-batching (low latency, small batches), continuous batching (higher throughput, better GPU utilization). For HarborPay where p95<200ms is required, we usually recommend micro-batching with adaptive timers plus a small headroom for bursts
[02:30] Carlos Ruiz: what about batch sizes, like 8 vs 32 — how does that map to latency?
[02:44] Rishi Patel: in practice, on an A100-class GPU, batch 8 gives near line-rate with ~10-15% latency overhead, batch 32 improves throughput but p95 jumps — we'd model it: single-token gen baseline, then add batching overhead. The KV cache reduces the number of tokens you actually have to compute per request which often outweighs batching gains for short requests
[03:10] Maya Lin: okay so KV cache seems crucial for us because we have that prefix reuse
[03:18] Lina Gomez: can you explain prefix vs kv cache? I get them mixed up sometimes
[03:25] Rishi Patel: yeah, quick: prefix cache stores the compressed representation of the common prompt prefix so the model doesn't re-run the first N tokens; KV cache stores key/value pairs for recent tokens during generation to avoid recomputing attention for earlier tokens. In Redwood's runtime we use both: prefix cache for shared static prefixes across many sessions, KV cache for intra-request caching during autoregressive decode.
[03:50] Rishi Patel: rough math: say average prompt 120 tokens with 50-token shared prefix. If prefix cache hits 60% of requests, you'd save recomputing 30 tokens on average; that directly reduces GPU work and cost
[04:10] Carlos Ruiz: can you show the cost model please?
[04:15] Rishi Patel: yep, pulling up slide — okay example baseline: hosted medium model cost $X per 1M tokens (we showed internal numbers), for demonstration assume $10 / 1M tokens. With batching and no cache, you might reduce per-token infra cost by 10-20% via utilization. Add prefix cache hit-rate 60% and effective compute tokens drop to ~70% -> cost down to ~$7 / 1M
[04:42] Priya Sharma: those are hosted numbers — if we go Dedicated, what's the delta? We have predictable traffic so dedicated might be cheaper per token but has infra and commit costs
[04:55] Ava Martinez: right — Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and better unit economics at scale. Our back-of-envelope: if you commit to a monthly pool that covers your 2k qps baseline, effective cost can drop 30-50% versus hosted depending on utilization and model. But there's an up-front commit and configuration for autoscale/burst.
[05:20] Maya Lin: what about cold starts and rotation? We need rolling updates with minimal disruption, and ability to fallback to smaller models under pressure
[05:30] Rishi Patel: Redwood supports canary rollouts and automatic fallback to compatible model variants, and routing policies by latency/cost/region. For dedicated, we can keep a hot-standby pool. For Private, it's similar but customer-managed infra
[05:50] Carlos Ruiz: security: SSO, KMS, audit logs — we need SOC2 artifacts before pilots
[05:58] Ava Martinez: we'll send SOC2 + ISO and the KMS integration docs after the call, Lina will include the key mapping patterns for HarborPay's HSM
[06:10] Maya Lin: good, thanks
[06:18] Rishi Patel: back to caching— prefix eviction policy matters. If your prefix set is large, hit-rate goes down. We recommend identifying top-100 prefixes (you mentioned you have ~20 common ones) and pin them to the cache. That gives diminishing returns after ~200 prefixes
[06:40] Lina Gomez: what's the memory footprint? We have constrained GPU memory on some nodes
[06:45] Rishi Patel: prefix cache is stored in RAM and can also be serialized; KV cache lives on the inference worker's memory during decode. Typical numbers: a 1k-token prefix vector for a 7B model is ~5-20MB depending on quantization. For 200 prefixes you'd be looking at a few GB total — configurable and can be offloaded in Dedicated setups
[07:10] Maya Lin: ok that fits our infra
[07:16] Rishi Patel: now demo of a simple cost table — imagine 1M requests/day, average 120 tokens, baseline 120M tokens/day. With 60% prefix hits and 30% token reduction from kv caching you get effective tokens ~60M. If hosted cost $10/1M -> $600/day -> $18k/month vs dedicated estimate $9k/month (example). These are illustrative — we'll run your real traces for a proper projection
[08:00] Carlos Ruiz: can you capture tail latency in the model? If caching reduces compute per request but introduces lookup latency, p95 might shift
[08:12] Rishi Patel: yes, cache lookup is typically microseconds on local memory; the main source of tail is batching/queueing. We model queuing delay with traffic profiles and adaptive batch timers. For p95 200ms target we tune batch timers smaller and keep some reserved capacity which increases unit cost slightly
[08:38] Maya Lin: what's the integration effort? SDKs, agents, or do we need to refactor our inference clients
[08:45] Ava Martinez: usually integration is a few endpoints calls if you use hosted API. For Dedicated/Private, we provide deployment templates and a small agent; typical integration time 2-6 weeks depending on SSO/KMS work and any network firewalling
[09:02] Priya Sharma: can the prefix cache be populated with historical data? We have logs of common prompts
[09:08] Rishi Patel: yes you can pre-seed the cache; best to seed top prefixes, and we can run an offline analysis to pick top-100 prefixes and estimated hit-rates — that is one of Rishi's next steps
[09:22] Lina Gomez: any pitfalls? We've seen regression on output quality when quantizing too aggressively
[09:28] Rishi Patel: good callout— quantization and aggressive batching can change behavior slightly; Redwood Optimize includes eval hooks and A/B rollouts so you can monitor quality regressions tied to prompt sets. We also recommend running a small eval suite pre/post changes
[09:45] Carlos Ruiz: network egress costs if we go hosted — do you have numbers?
[09:50] Ava Martinez: egress depends on region and provider; we'll include a breakout in the pricing deck. For many customers egress is smaller than compute cost but we won't hide it
[10:05] Maya Lin: let's talk pilot design — what do you need from us to run the KV cache cost model?
[10:12] Rishi Patel: ideally: 7-day request logs (timestamps, prompt hash, request length, response length), sample of top prefix texts, and your SLOs. We can take logs and run a simulation to estimate hit-rate and token-savings. We map that into hosted vs dedicated cost curves
[10:30] Maya Lin: we can share logs internally, security approved, I'll follow up with Lina
[10:36] Priya Sharma: how do you handle PII in sample logs? We can't send raw user data
[10:40] Lina Gomez: redwood: we have scrubbing tools, you can hash or redact tokens, we only need prompt shapes and counts, not raw contents. We'll send a template for scrubbed logs
[10:52] Rishi Patel: demo time — quick screen share, here's the KV cache model spreadsheet; column A: prefix hit-rate, column B: avg tokens saved, column C: effective tokens, column D: cost per 1M, column E: latency impact
[11:10] Rishi Patel: as you slide hit-rate from 0 to 80% you can see cost drop nonlinearly; big wins early if you have a small number of hot prefixes
[11:25] Carlos Ruiz: can we apply this per-route? Some routes are longer form and shouldn't be cached
[11:30] Rishi Patel: yes, per-route policies are best practice — pin short system prompts and signup flows to cache, leave free-form completion routes uncached
[11:40] Maya Lin: what's the typical timeline to pilot?
[11:44] Ava Martinez: with cleaned logs we can deliver a model-run in ~3 business days and an initial pilot setup in 2 weeks assuming SSO & network work go smoothly
[11:52] Priya Sharma: ok, that's reasonable
[12:00] Maya Lin: any final questions?
[12:05] Carlos Ruiz: one more on fallback — if dedicated pool saturates does Redwood reroute to hosted automatically?
[12:12] Rishi Patel: yes, routing policy can fallback to hosted or smaller model. You can set hard limits and failover thresholds. We'll show policy examples in the follow-up doc
[12:25] Ava Martinez: recap — next steps: Ava send pricing and SOC2/ISO docs, Rishi run KV cost model on your scrubbed logs, Maya to provide logs and top prefixes, schedule pilot week of Apr 20. We'll also include a sample canary rollout config and fallback policy
[12:45] Maya Lin: great thanks everyone
[12:48] Priya Sharma: thanks, talk soon
[12:50] Ava Martinez: thanks, bye

Notes: transcription contains minor mis-hears (e.g., model names abbreviated), timestamps approximate. Links shared during call: KV cache model spreadsheet (link), Redwood SOC2 doc (link), Pricing deck (link).
